## Sections
- ○ Summary

## Summary

<!-- PLACEHOLDER:summary -->
_Synthesize the spec in 2-3 sentences: what changes, why it matters, for whom._

## Problem Statement

<!-- PLACEHOLDER:problem-statement -->
_Describe the current pain: what is broken, missing, or inefficient? For whom? What happens today when they try?_

## Ambition

<!-- PLACEHOLDER:ambition -->
_What does success look like? Paint the 12-month ideal state — not just this feature, but the trajectory it starts._

## Reversibility

<!-- PLACEHOLDER:reversibility -->
_If this ships and is wrong, how do we undo it? Rollback steps, feature flags, migration reversibility, blast radius._

## User Impact

<!-- PLACEHOLDER:user-impact -->
_Who benefits and how? What changes for them — before/after their day, their workflow, their frustration?_

## Verification Strategy

<!-- PLACEHOLDER:verification-strategy -->
_How will we know it worked? Automated tests, manual smoke tests, metrics to watch, acceptance checklist._

## Scope Boundary

<!-- PLACEHOLDER:scope-boundary -->
_What is explicitly OUT of scope? Name specific features, use cases, or edge cases this spec does NOT address._

## Premises

<!-- PLACEHOLDER:premises -->
_List every assumption this spec makes. If an assumption turns out wrong, what breaks?_

## Tasks

<!-- PLACEHOLDER:tasks -->
_Break implementation into concrete tasks. Each task: what it does, how to verify it is done, any ordering constraints._

## Acceptance Criteria

<!-- PLACEHOLDER:acceptance-criteria -->
_Binary, testable criteria. Each item: the system does X when Y. No fuzzy language._

{
  "phase": "DISCOVERY",
  "instruction": "Conduct a thorough discovery conversation. FIRST: perform a pre-discovery codebase scan (README, CLAUDE.md, recent git log, TODOs, directory structure) and present a brief audit summary. THEN: challenge the user's spec description against your findings. THEN: ask the unanswered discovery questions together, offering concrete options based on codebase knowledge, and register a follow-up for each unclear answer with `npx eser@latest noskills spec settings-page followup <questionId> \"question\"` before you submit; noskills then gives you each follow-up on its own. AFTER questions: present a dream state table (current → this spec → future), scored expansion proposals, architectural decisions, and an error/rescue map. FINALLY: present a complete discovery synthesis for user confirmation before submitting answers as a JSON object.",
  "questions": [
    {
      "id": "status_quo",
      "text": "What does the user do today without this feature?",
      "concerns": [
        "product:status_quo",
        "eng:replace_scope",
        "qa:regression_risk"
      ],
      "extras": []
    },
    {
      "id": "ambition",
      "text": "Describe the 1-star and 10-star versions.",
      "concerns": [
        "product:scope_direction",
        "eng:complexity_tier",
        "qa:test_depth"
      ],
      "extras": []
    },
    {
      "id": "reversibility",
